title: CLAUDE.md
text: nhsbsa low-level R client NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) Open Data Portal — standard CKAN catalogue https://opendata.nhsbsa.net/api/3/action/. generic client domain knowledge: functions wrap CKAN API actions one--one return plain data (tibbles tabular results, lists metadata). Callers supply dataset identifiers interpret results; domain-specific logic belongs separate consumer package, .

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Purity. One exported function per CKAN action, named , argument every documented API parameter, users familiar API need relearn anything. deliberate exceptions two convenience helpers nhsbsa_list_resources() nhsbsa_download_resource(). One request layer. Every endpoint thin caller nhsbsa_query() (R/core.R), reads calling function’s arguments query string, performs request retry/backoff, validates CKAN envelope fails gracefully portal unreachable. Portal quirks (documented relevant): datastore identifies resource name (e.g. EPD_201401), UUID; datastore_search_sql requires resource_id alongside sql nests records one level deeper standard CKAN.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: UK English throughout (e.g. “serialise”, “behaviour”, “parameterise”). snake_case; exported functions prefixed nhsbsa_. Use cli via internal wrappers nhsbsa_abort() / nhsbsa_warn() / nhsbsa_inform() (R/conditions.R) — never another package’s error helpers. Give conditions specific subclasses can handled programmatically. HTTP via httr2. Prefer tidyverse (dplyr, purrr, stringr, tibble) reads well; use base R genuinely simpler.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Tests use testthat (edition 3). Network tests replay recorded httptest2 fixtures run offline; live API tests gated behind NHSBSA_LIVE_TESTS. devtools::test() — run tests (set NHSBSA_LIVE_TESTS=true include live). lintr::lint_package() — lint. air format . — format. devtools::document() — regenerate docs. devtools::check() — R CMD check. spelling::spell_check_package() — UK English spell check. recording new fixtures, keep with_mock_dir() directory names short: fixed opendata.nhsbsa.net/api/3/action/ path deep, long names can push tarball paths portable 100-byte limit.

title: Developer guide
text: nhsbsa low-level, general-purpose client NHS Business Services Authority Open Data Portal, CKAN catalogue. Two principles shape every decision: Purity. one exported function per CKAN action, named , argument every documented API parameter. user knows CKAN API learn anything new. deliberate exceptions two convenience helpers nhsbsa_list_resources() nhsbsa_download_resource(). “exceptions” , unlike every exported function, neither corresponds single CKAN action: nhsbsa_list_resources() calls nhsbsa_package_show() reshapes nested resources list tibble, nhsbsa_download_resource() resolves resource (via nhsbsa_package_show()) streams file url — ordinary HTTP download part /action/ API . earn place together operations caller often needs. domain knowledge. package knows nothing specific datasets (BNF, prescribing, dental, ). returns plain data — tibbles tabular results, lists metadata — leaves interpretation caller. Dataset-specific logic belongs separate package depends one.

title: Developer guide
text: package thin shell around single request layer.
code: endpoint functions  ->  nhsbsa_query()  ->  httr2  ->  CKAN    (R/package.R,         (R/core.R)     resources.R,     datastore.R,     catalogue.R)

title: Developer guide
text: nhsbsa_query(action) work: inspects calling endpoint function rlang::caller_fn() rlang::fn_fmls_names(), reads argument values caller’s environment, turns query parameters. Arguments prefixed . (.return_raw) reserved client behaviour never sent API. Values coerced CKAN nhsbsa_format_query_value(): NULLs dropped, logicals become "true"/"false", multi-element vectors joined commas, lists (filters) encoded JSON. request performed retry/backoff. nhsbsa_perform() translates transport failures graceful nhsbsa_offline error HTTP errors nhsbsa_api_error (plus status-specific subclass nhsbsa_http_404). CKAN envelope validated: success = FALSE raises nhsbsa_api_error; otherwise returns result element (, caller passed .return_raw = TRUE, whole parsed envelope). parameters read function signature, endpoint wrapper usually single line — see .

title: Developer guide
text: messages, warnings errors go nhsbsa_abort(), nhsbsa_warn() nhsbsa_inform(). wrap corresponding cli functions, always append base class (nhsbsa_error / nhsbsa_warning / nhsbsa_message), accept optional class prepend specific subclass. Give condition specific subclass whenever caller might reasonably want catch , e.g. call cli::cli_abort() (package’s error helpers) directly.
code: nhsbsa_abort(   c("x" = "No resource matched."),   class = "nhsbsa_resource_not_found" )

title: Developer guide
text: Catalogue/metadata actions return list (package_show, package_search, resource_show). Listing actions return character vector (package_list, organization_list, group_list, tag_list). Row queries return tibble (datastore_search, datastore_search_sql, list_resources). nhsbsa_download_resource() returns destination path invisibly. read-function called .return_raw = TRUE returns parsed envelope list.

title: Developer guide
text: portal exposes standard CKAN read API (can confirm given instance supports help_show, e.g. https://opendata.nhsbsa.net/api/3/action/help_show?name=package_search). package wraps useful read subset actions — dataset discovery, resource listing/metadata/download, datastore queries, catalogue listings. registered actions (*_autocomplete family, datastore_info, license_list, status_show, ) intentionally wrapped yet. gap discovered, convention open issue add wrapper .

title: Developer guide
text: wrap another CKAN action, add thin function whose arguments mirror API parameters. example, wrap tag_show: whole implementation: nhsbsa_query() picks id signature sends query parameter. action returns tabular data, post-process result nhsbsa_records_to_tibble(). : Keep examples gated @examplesIf identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true") render documentation site never run CRAN.

The tag name or id. #' @inheritParams nhsbsa_package_list #' #' @return A list of tag metadata. #' @export #' @examplesIf identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true") #' nhsbsa_tag_show("prescribing") nhsbsa_tag_show <- function(id, .return_raw = FALSE) {   nhsbsa_query("tag_show") } devtools::document() # regenerate NAMESPACE and the .Rd file

title: Getting started with nhsbsa
text: NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) Open Data Portal publishes open datasets NHS activity England — prescribing, dental, pharmaceutical contractor data among . freely available Open Government Licence. portal runs CKAN, widely used open-source data catalogue. CKAN organises data datasets (called “packages”) contain one resources — individual files (usually CSV) can download, , tabular resources, query row row. nhsbsa thin, low-level client portal. wraps CKAN API returns plain data work : tibbles tabular results lists metadata. contains knowledge particular dataset, supply dataset identifiers interpret results . familiar CKAN API, package feel familiar : function names arguments mirror API.

what: The API and the response envelope
title: Getting started with nhsbsa
text: Every request goes CKAN action comes back JSON envelope form , failure, nhsbsa handles envelope : checks success flag, returns result, otherwise raises informative error. portal reached (example internet connection) fails gracefully clear message rather obscure low-level error. full set actions documented CKAN Action API reference, portal return documentation individual action supports, e.g. https://opendata.nhsbsa.net/api/3/action/help_show?name=datastore_search_sql.
code: https://opendata.nhsbsa.net/api/3/action/<action> { "success": true, "result": ... } { "success": false, "error": { "message": "..." } }

title: Getting started with nhsbsa
text: package wraps useful read subset portal’s actions, four small groups (package reference index organised way). need action yet wrapped, please open issue. Datasets — discover inspect datasets (“packages”): nhsbsa_package_list() (every dataset id), nhsbsa_package_search() (search), nhsbsa_package_show() (one dataset’s metadata, including resources). Resources — work files dataset: nhsbsa_resource_show() (one resource’s metadata), plus two convenience helpers, nhsbsa_list_resources() nhsbsa_download_resource(). Datastore — query rows tabular resource without downloading : nhsbsa_datastore_search() nhsbsa_datastore_search_sql(). Catalogue — list portal’s taxonomy: nhsbsa_organization_list(), nhsbsa_group_list() nhsbsa_tag_list(). Almost every function maps one--one onto CKAN action name. two exceptions resource helpers, combine action little extra work pure wrappers: nhsbsa_list_resources() calls nhsbsa_package_show() reshapes nested resources tibble — one row per file, including file’s download url. nhsbsa_download_resource() resolves single resource (via nhsbsa_package_show()) streams resource’s file url disk. download ordinary HTTP request, CKAN action. (nhsbsa_group_list() included completeness; portal currently defines groups returns empty vector — organises data organisation tags instead.) read-functions also accept .return_raw = TRUE, returns full parsed response envelope instead processed result — useful need fields helper surface, datastore query’s total.

title: Getting started with nhsbsa
text: helps think package programmatic version portal website. things click map onto API calls: Browsing datasets nhsbsa_package_list() (identifiers) nhsbsa_package_search() (richer records, searching paging). Clicking tag, say #Prescribing, takes website /dataset/?tags=Prescribing. filter query tags field returns datasets carrying tag: returns datasets website shows tag, website’s dataset view hides Freedom Information disclosure log default. match website displays, exclude organisation well. result list, whose results element holds one record per dataset; pull title compare website: Tags case-sensitive; list nhsbsa_tag_list(), organisations can filter nhsbsa_organization_list(). Opening dataset’s page (e.g. /dataset/english-prescribing-data-epd) corresponds nhsbsa_package_show("english-prescribing-data-epd"), whose resources element lists files shown page. nhsbsa_list_resources() tidies resources tibble. “Download” button resource fetches file nhsbsa_download_resource() streams disk; data preview / “Data API” resource backed datastore nhsbsa_datastore_search() queries.

title: Getting started with nhsbsa
text: nhsbsa_datastore_search() returns rows resource. can choose order columns fields, sort sort, page limit/offset. Field names case-sensitive must match resource’s columns exactly (EPD upper case, e.g. PCO_CODE): datastore returns one page rows per request. rows exist returned, nhsbsa_datastore_search() warns explains page rest increasing offset: CKAN’s datastore_search also defines filters (exact field matching) q (full-text search) parameters, nhsbsa_datastore_search() exposes completeness. aware portal’s datastore apply — return matching rows — filter value, use SQL instead.
code: nhsbsa_datastore_search(   resource_id = "EPD_202401",   fields = c("PCO_CODE", "BNF_CHEMICAL_SUBSTANCE", "ITEMS"),   sort = "ITEMS desc",   limit = 5 ) #> Warning: ! Retrieved 5 of 18080573 matching rows; 18080568 not returned. #> ℹ Fetch the next page with `offset = 5` (reusing your other arguments), #>   increasing `offset` until all rows are retrieved. #> ℹ Raising `limit` returns more rows per request, up to the server-side maximum. #> # A tibble: 5 × 3 #>   PCO_CODE BNF_CHEMICAL_SUBSTANCE ITEMS #>   <chr>    <chr>                  <int> #> 1 11J00    1404000H0               3584 #> 2 06H00    0212000B0               3571 #> 3 02Y00    0212000B0               3469 #> 4 12F00    1404000H0               3160 #> 5 11M00    1404000H0               3038 nhsbsa_datastore_search(   resource_id = "EPD_202401",   fields = c("PCO_CODE", "ITEMS"),   limit = 5,   offset = 5 ) #> Warning: ! title: Getting started with nhsbsa
text: nhsbsa_datastore_search_sql() runs read-SQL query, reliable way filter, compute expressions, aggregate sort portal. portal requires resource_id alongside query, reference resource name clause: SQL string sent API verbatim, responsible paging (via LIMIT/OFFSET) quoting identifiers correctly.
code: # Filter to one organisation nhsbsa_datastore_search_sql(   resource_id = "EPD_202401",   sql = "SELECT PCO_CODE, BNF_CHEMICAL_SUBSTANCE, ITEMS          FROM `EPD_202401`          WHERE PCO_CODE = 'W2U3Z'          LIMIT 5" ) #> # A tibble: 5 × 3 #>   PCO_CODE BNF_CHEMICAL_SUBSTANCE ITEMS #>   <chr>    <chr>                  <int> #> 1 W2U3Z    0913011N0                  4 #> 2 W2U3Z    0703021Q0                  1 #> 3 W2U3Z    0408010H0                  4 #> 4 W2U3Z    0601022B0                  1 #> 5 W2U3Z    0906040G0                  1 # Aggregate: total items prescribed per organisation nhsbsa_datastore_search_sql(   resource_id = "EPD_202401",   sql = "SELECT PCO_CODE, SUM(ITEMS) AS items          FROM `EPD_202401`          GROUP BY PCO_CODE          ORDER BY items DESC          LIMIT 5" ) #> # A tibble: 5 × 2 #>   PCO_CODE   items #>   <chr>      <int> #> 1 91Q00    3151968 #> 2 W2U3Z    3129964 #> 3 A3A8R    3124609 #> 4 D9Y0V    2697474 #> 5 15N00    2413359

Dataset Description

Prescription Cost Analysis (PCA) shows the total volume and cost for drugs, dressings, appliances, and medical devices that have been dispensed in the community in England and submitted to the NHSBSA for reimbursement monthly. 

This dataset is designed to provide the total number of prescription items and spend for any individual product, at any level of the British National Formulary (BNF) hierarchy. For example, for Paracetamol 500mg tablets, or collections of products such as antibacterial drugs, antidepressant drugs, or dressings. 

This data mirrors the methodology used in the PCA Annual National Statistics publication.  

The latest statistical release, along with more information on what PCA contains, can be found on the NHSBSA website and you can specifically read the Prescription Cost Analysis Background Information and Methodology. The monthly PCA release is a monthly management information data set and is not an Official Statistic. 

Data for February 2008 to March 2021 is available on the NHSBSA website in a legacy format. 

Overview of Service

Information about our NHSBSA Prescriptions Data service can be found here - Prescription data | NHSBSA

Dataset Details

Data Source

NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) Data Warehouse.

Data Collection

The dataset is provided from Prescription data collected by the NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) for the operational purpose of reimbursing and remunerating dispensing contractors for the costs of supplying drugs and devices, and providing essential and advanced services, to NHS patients. The data that forms the basis of these statistics is collected as a by-product of this process.

Time Periods

Data is published retrospectively with a two-month delay. For example, January data is published in March.

Historical Data: Data is available from January 2021 onwards.

Geography

The PCA dataset is limited to a view of items dispensed only in the community in England, regardless of whether they were prescribed in England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland, and State authorities such as Guernsey, Jersey, Alderney, and Isle of Man.

Statistical Classification

Management Information - This is not an official statistic.

Caveats

Information:

Excluded Items

The dataset does not include items that were not dispensed, were disallowed, or were returned to the contractor for further clarification.
Information:

Prescribing Contexts Not Included

Prescriptions that are prescribed and dispensed within prisons, hospitals, or issued as private prescriptions are not included in this dataset.
Information:

Unsubmitted or Unclaimed Items

Items that were prescribed but either not presented for dispensing, or not submitted to NHS Prescription Services by the dispenser, are also excluded.
Information:

Further Information

Additional limitations of the dataset can be found in the Prescription Cost Analysis Background Information and Methodology.

Enquiries

Who can I contact if I have queries relating to the data?

If you have any queries regarding the data provided, or if you plan on publishing the data, please contact DataServicesSupport@nhsbsa.nhs.uk ensuring you quote the name of the dataset for reference. This is important to ensure that the figures are not misunderstood or misrepresented.

Citing and Reusing This Data

Important information regarding reusing the data and copyright

If you plan on producing a press or broadcast story based upon the data, please contact communicationsteam@nhsbsa.nhs.uk. This is important to ensure that the figures are not misunderstood or misrepresented.

The information supplied to you continues to be protected by the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 and/or other applicable law. You may use the data freely, provided that you attribute the source.

Important: 2026-05-11: Change to SNOMED_CODE Data Type

The SNOMED_CODE field has been changed from numeric to string for all files in this dataset from November 2020 onwards, including future releases, to preserve the full code value. SNOMED codes are identifiers (not numbers for calculation), and storing them as numeric can result in formatting issues such as trailing zeros.

This change ensures codes are stored exactly as intended. Users may need to update any processes that previously treated this field as numeric. If you have previously included SNOMED codes in your analysis or reporting, you are advised to re-run your outputs.

Important: 2026-04-22: ICB Naming Update (Effective from February 2026 Data Files)

Sub‑location names in this dataset use the 2026/27 ICB naming (as per the NHS Digital change summary) rather than the 2025/26 SICBL names. For example, NHS Surrey Heartlands ICB appears as NHS Surrey and Sussex ICB. Only the names have been updated — the underlying organisational structure remains that of 2025/26.

Read the full news article for further details.

Dataset Description

The English Prescribing Dataset (EPD) is a comprehensive monthly dataset capturing all prescriptions issued by NHS primary care prescribers in England and dispensed in the community. This includes prescriptions from GPs, nurses, and other authorised primary care prescribers. The dataset is openly available via the NHS Business Services Authority’s (NHSBSA) Open Data Portal, promoting transparency and enabling widespread analysis.

With approximately 17 million rows of data added each month, the EPD provides one of the most detailed views of NHS prescribing activity of England. It is a crucial resource for analysing prescribing trends, costs, and behaviours at both national and local levels.

Key Features

  • Practice-Level Information: Each record is linked to a specific NHS GP practice or primary care organisation, enabling local-level analysis.
  • BNF and SNOMED CT Codes: Prescriptions are classified using Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT), British National Formulary (BNF) codes, and Dictionary of Medicines and Devices (dm+d), ensuring standardised identification and interoperability across NHS systems.
  • Prescription Costs: Captures the financial cost associated with each prescription, reflecting reimbursement claims.
  • Quantities Dispensed: Provides data on the volume of items prescribed and dispensed.
  • Data Granularity: The dataset offers detailed insights down to the individual prescription level, allowing in-depth analyses of prescribing patterns and trends.

Dataset Details

Additional Dataset Guidance: Further details on this dataset can be found in the English Prescribing Dataset Release Guidance (ODT: 237KB).

Use Cases and Benefits

The EPD supports a range of users, including healthcare professionals, policy-makers, and researchers. Key applications include:

  • Healthcare Research: Enables analysis of prescribing patterns, medication usage, and adherence to clinical guidelines across different regions and demographics.
  • Service Planning: Helps NHS organisations identify prescribing trends, evaluate costs, and assess policy impacts.
  • Public Health Monitoring: Tracks national health priorities, such as antibiotic usage, controlled drug prescriptions, and emerging treatments.
  • Optimising NHS Resources: Supports data-driven decision-making to improve prescribing cost-effectiveness.
  • Digital Healthcare Alignment: Enhances interoperability by integrating with NHS England’s digital health strategy.
  • Integration with Other Datasets: Can be linked with hospital episode statistics, public health records, and other datasets to provide a more comprehensive view of patient care and prescribing impacts.

Supporting Healthcare Objectives

The dataset provides unique insights into prescribing behaviours, enabling:

  • Monitoring of health inequalities by examining regional prescribing trends.
  • Evaluation of guideline adherence, such as the reduction of high-risk medications.
  • Promotion of cost-effective prescribing through analysis of generic vs. branded medications.
  • Antimicrobial stewardship by tracking antibiotic prescriptions and other key drug classes.
Overview of Service

Information about our NHSBSA Prescriptions Data service can be found here - Prescription data | NHSBSA

Data Source

NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) Data Warehouse.

Data collection

The English Prescribing Dataset (EPD) is compiled from multiple NHSBSA data sources to ensure accuracy and consistency in prescription records.

  • BNF Data: Sourced from the NHSBSA drug database, which maintains the British National Formulary (BNF) classification system as implemented prior to edition 70.
  • SNOMED CT Data: Extracted from the NHSBSA drug database, ensuring alignment with standardised clinical terminology.
  • Organisational Data: Derived from the NHSBSA organisational database, providing up-to-date information on NHS GP practices and primary care organisations.
  • Prescription Data: Includes all prescription items prescribed in the community in England and submitted to NHSBSA for reimbursement and remuneration by dispensing contractors on a monthly basis.

Time Periods

Publication Frequency: Data is uploaded monthly, typically around the 20th, following the NHSBSA prescription data refresh.

Data is published retrospectively with a two-month delay. For example, January data is published in March.

Historical Data: Records covering January 2014 to June 2025 are available within the now retired English Prescribing Dataset (EPD) without SNOMED CT codes

Geography

Prescriptions issued in England that have been dispensed in England, Wales, Scotland, Guernsey, Alderney, Jersey, and the Isle of Man.

Caveats

Information:

Data Structure and Code changes

The SNOMED CT and BNF codes linked to a product may change over time. As the dataset is static, the codes within each report are only relevant to the specific month of publication.

More detailed information on the BNF hierarchical structure is available for reference (BNF Code Information Historic Dataset on the NHSBSA Open Data Portal). However, this data is taken from a different date point and does not directly align with the EPD dataset.

Information:

Exclusion of Medicines Supplied Under Patient Group Directions (PGDs)

The EPD dataset does not capture any medicines that are supplied under PGDs, (structured protocols allowing specific healthcare professionals (like pharmacists) to supply or administer medicines without a prescription). Services operating under PGDs that are excluded from EPD:

  • Pharmacy First Clinical Pathways (PFCP) – e.g. treatments for minor ailments
  • Contraception services
  • Smoking cessation support
  • Urgent medicines supply
  • Seasonal flu vaccinations

These services are tracked separately. For more insights into these areas:

  • Pharmacy First data: NHS Pharmacy First Clinical Pathways Data | NHSBSA
  • Other pharmacy services: Dispensing data | NHSBSA
  • Flu service reporting: Flu report - Oracle Analytics Dashboard
Information:

Exclusion of Dental Prescribing

Prescriptions issued by dentists and dispensed in the community are not included in the EPD dataset.

Information:

Hospital Prescribing: Site Code vs. Cost Centre

There is a distinction in hospital prescribing data included in EPD:

  • Excluded: Items prescribed using Hospital Site codes and dispensed in the community
  • Included: Items prescribed using Hospital Cost Centre codes, even if dispensed in the community

This means that although both may represent hospital-originated prescriptions, only those tied to cost centres are within EPD scope. For further analysis of Hospital Site code prescribing, refer to the Hospital Prescribing Dispensed in the Community Dataset, which excludes Hospital Cost Centre data to avoid duplication.

Information:

Financial Data Methodology

From April 2024 (data published from June 2024), actual cost calculations in financial reports will include discounts calculated under a new methodology. Further details can be found in the article: Changes to Actual Cost reporting calculation (Pharmacy only).

Information:

SNOMED CT and BNF Code Mapping

More detailed mapping of medicine and appliance products with their associated SNOMED CT and BNF codes is available at BNF SNOMED mapping | NHSBSA. The timing of these reports is aligned to the monthly EPD dataset.

Dataset Description

This ad hoc release provides information on prescriptions prescribed in England and dispensed in Scotland monthly between June 2023 and June 2024.

The NHSBSA receive prescription data from NHS Scotland of English prescribing dispensed in Scotland and is held in the NHSBSA Data Warehouse.

This dataset is published within the English Prescribing Data (EPD) – NHSBSA, however, due to technical issues, June 2023 - June 2024 of prescribing data has not been included. To support users who may require this information NHSBSA have made this available as an ad hoc release.

Prescription data from July 2024 onwards will begin to reappear in the English Prescribing Dataset from September 2024 data release.

Alternatively, this can be obtained from ePACT2 | NHSBSA provided you have access to create your own analysis, further information on gaining access and any training requirements can be found by Registering for ePACT2 | NHSBSA.

Overview of Service

Information about our NHSBSA Prescriptions Data service can be found here – Prescription data | NHSBSA.

Dataset Details

Data Source

NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) Data Warehouse from data provided by NHS Scotland.

Data Collection

The dataset is provided from prescription data collected by NHS Scotland and sent to the NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA).

Public Health Scotland.

Time Periods

This dataset is for the period June 2023 to June 2024.

Geography

This dataset is based on items that have been prescribed in England (only) and dispensed in the community in Scotland.

Statistical Classification

Management information - This is not an official statistic.

Caveats

Information: Cost Comparisons
The NIC and Actual Costs in the dataset provided by NHS Scotland may be different to the NIC and Actual Costs for the same products and quantities dispensed in England.
Information: Geographic Coverage
The data excludes prescriptions issued in Wales, Scotland, Guernsey, Alderney, Jersey, and the Isle of Man.
Information: Data Exclusions
The dataset excludes any patient-identifiable data; items not dispensed, disallowed, or returned to the contractor for clarification; prescriptions issued and dispensed in Prisons, Hospitals, or as Private prescriptions; and items prescribed but not presented for dispensing or not submitted to NHS Prescription Services by the dispenser.

Enquiries

Who can I contact if I have queries relating to the data?

If you have any queries regarding the data provided, or if you plan on publishing the data, please contact DataServicesSupport@nhsbsa.nhs.uk ensuring you quote the name of the dataset for reference. This is important to ensure that the figures are not misunderstood or misrepresented.

Citing and Reusing This Data

Important information regarding reusing the data and copyright

If you plan on producing a press or broadcast story based upon the data, please contact communicationsteam@nhsbsa.nhs.uk. This is important to ensure that the figures are not misunderstood or misrepresented.

The information supplied to you continues to be protected by the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 and/or other applicable law. You may use the data freely, provided that you attribute the source.

https://opendata.nhsbsa.net/dataset/english-prescribing-dataset-epd-with-snomed-code This now retired dataset contains information on prescriptions issued in England that have been dispensed in England, Wales, Scotland, Guernsey, Alderney, Jersey, and the Isle of Man. The dataset combines elements of the Detailed Prescribing Information (DPI) data previously released by NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) via the Information Services Portal, and the [Practice Level Prescribing in England (PLP)](https://digital.nhs.uk/data-and-information/publications/statistical/practice-level-prescribing-data) data released by NHS Digital via their website. It is intended to replace both of those sources. These datasets have been brought together to provide end users with a single comprehensive, consistent and accessible source of prescribing information. Find out more about this data in the guidance document: [English Prescribing Dataset guidance document (ODT): 233KB](https://github.com/NHSBSA-Open-Data/OPD/raw/main/English%20Prescribing%20Dataset%20Release%20Guidance%20v003.odt) [English Prescribing Dataset guidance document (PDF):238KB](https://github.com/NHSBSA-Open-Data/OPD/raw/main/English%20Prescribing%20Dataset%20Release%20Guidance%20v003.pdf)

Overview of Service

Information about our NHSBSA Prescriptions Data service can be found here - Prescription data | NHSBSA

Dataset Details

Data Source

NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) Data Warehouse.

Data collection

The English Prescribing Dataset (EPD) is compiled from multiple NHSBSA data sources to ensure accuracy and consistency in prescription records.

  • BNF Data: Sourced from the NHSBSA drug database, which maintains the British National Formulary (BNF) classification system as implemented prior to edition 70.
  • Organisational Data: Derived from the NHSBSA organisational database, providing up-to-date information on NHS GP practices and primary care organisations.
  • Prescription Data: Includes all prescription items prescribed in the community in England and submitted to NHSBSA for reimbursement and remuneration by dispensing contractors on a monthly basis.

Time Periods

Publication Frequency: Data is uploaded monthly, typically around the 20th, following the NHSBSA prescription data refresh.

Data is published retrospectively with a two-month delay. For example, January data is published in March.

Historical Data: Records are available from January 2014 onwards.

Geography

Prescriptions issued in England that have been dispensed in England, Wales, Scotland, Guernsey, Alderney, Jersey, and the Isle of Man.

Caveats

Information:

Exclusion of Medicines Supplied Under Patient Group Directions (PGDs)

The EPD dataset does not capture any medicines that are supplied under PGDs, ( structured protocols allowing specific healthcare professionals (like pharmacists) to supply or administer medicines without a prescription). Services operating under PGDs that are excluded from EPD:

  • Pharmacy First Clinical Pathways (PFCP) – e.g. treatments for minor ailments
  • Contraception services
  • Smoking cessation support
  • Urgent medicines supply
  • Seasonal flu vaccinations

These services are tracked separately. For more insights into these areas:

  • Pharmacy First data: NHS Pharmacy First Clinical Pathways Data | NHSBSA
  • Other pharmacy services: Dispensing data | NHSBSA
  • Flu service reporting: Flu report - Oracle Analytics Dashboard
Information:

Exclusion of Dental Prescribing

Prescriptions issued by dentists and dispensed in the community are not included in the EPD dataset.

Information:

Hospital Prescribing: Site Code vs. Cost Centre

There is a distinction in hospital prescribing data included in EPD:

  • Excluded: Items prescribed using Hospital Site codes and dispensed in the community
  • Included: Items prescribed using Hospital Cost Centre codes, even if dispensed in the community

This means that although both may represent hospital-originated prescriptions, only those tied to cost centres are within EPD scope. For further analysis of Hospital Site code prescribing, refer to the Hospital Prescribing Dispensed in the Community Dataset, which excludes Hospital Cost Centre data to avoid duplication.

Enquiries

Who can I contact if I have queries relating to the data?

If you have any queries regarding the data provided, or if you plan on publishing, the data please contact DataServicesSupport@nhsbsa.nhs.uk ensuring you quote the name of the dataset for reference. This is important to ensure that the figures are not misunderstood or misrepresented.

If you plan on producing a press or broadcast story based upon the data please contact communicationsteam@nhsbsa.nhs.uk . This is important to ensure that the figures are not misunderstood or misrepresented.

If you consider any part of this request to exceed the appropriate cost threshold, please advise me of any data you are able to release within the cost limits. ##Response Pre-October 2022 I am writing to advise you that following a search of our paper and electronic records, I have established that the information you requested is not held by the NHSBSA. FP17 counts for Non-Molar and Molar Endodontic treatment began in October 2022. Therefore the figures for 2022/23 are from that month onwards. October 2022 Onwards I can confirm that the NHSBSA holds the information you have requested and a copy of the information and notes explaining it is attached. This report contains the details from General FP17s processed for the Reporting Years 2022/2023 (partial) & 2023/2024 for England Contracts. The data includes activity by Foundation Dentists. The information within the report includes the data items and descriptions listed below. Reporting Year: The financial year which the activity relate to. Year-end methodology will include all activity data (including amendments) collected from FP17s scheduled in any of the fifteen schedule months from April to June, where the date of completion is on or between 1 April and 31 March of the year. For example 2023/24 will include all activity data (including amendments) collected from FP17s scheduled in any of the fifteen schedule months from April 2023 to June 2024, where the date of completion is on or between 1 April 2023 and 31 March 2024. Where FP17s do not have a date of completion, e.g. where the patient has failed to return to complete the treatment, the date of acceptance is used. Contract Number: This is a unique 10 character number which identifies a contract. Commissioner Name: This is the name associated with the Commissioning Organisation. This is a generic term used to denote health bodies, either Area Teams in England or Health Boards in Wales. Also known as Primary Care Organisations (PCOs)). Region Description: Latest name associated with the Region. Provider Name: The name of the provider. PPC Location V Code: The V code associated with the Principle Practice and Correspondence Address. Molar Endodontic FP17s: Search results for forms where the Molar Endodontic box was ticked in part 5a of the FP17. Non-Molar Endodontic FP17s: Search results for forms where the Non-Molar Endodontic box was ticked in part 5a of the FP17. Treatment Charge Band: The patient charge band associated with a course of treatment as stated in Part 5 Treatment Category of the FP17. Here is the link to that https://opendata.nhsbsa.net/dataset/foi-01535 My question is, that for the year beginning April 1 2022 and ending April 2023, how many tooth extractions in England and Wales, carried out on adults and children, were extractions for braces? It would also be useful, if you carry the data, to see what purposes the tooth extractions were carried out for #Response# A copy of the information is attached. Please note we do not collect data regarding the number of teeth for Orthodontic extractions or the purpose for the extraction. Guidance notes This report contains the details from Orthodontic FP17Os processed for the reporting year 2022/2023 in England & Wales. The information within the report includes the data items and descriptions listed below. Activity by Foundation Dentists is excluded. Reporting Year: The financial year which the activity relates to. Year-end methodology will include all activity data (including amendments) collected from FP17Os scheduled in any of the fifteen schedule months from April to June, where the date of completion is on or between 1 April and 31 March of the year. For example, 2022-23 will include all activity data (including amendments) collected from FP17Os scheduled in any of the fifteen schedule months from April 2022 to June 2023, where the date of completion is on or between 1 April 2022 and 31 March 2023. Where FP17Os do not have a date of completion, e.g. where the patient has failed to return to complete the treatment, the date of acceptance is used. Country Name: This is the country the contract is located in. Orthodontic Treatment Starts: This is a count of the number of forms submitted where the assess and accept box has been ticked and the date treatment began has been entered on the FP17O. In effect, this is the number of treatment starts. Orthodontic Treatment Starts With Extractions (Orthodontic): This is a count of the number of orthodontic treatment starts submitted where the extractions box has been ticked on a FP17O. This is based on the orthodontic clinical data set as recorded in part 4 of the FP17. % Orthodontic Treatment Starts With Extractions (Orthodontic): This is the number of orthodontic treatment starts submitted where the extractions box has been ticked on a FP17O / Orthodontic Treatment Starts expressed as percentage. Orthodontic Treatment Completions: This is a count of the number of forms where the treatment completed box in part 6 of the FP17O has been ticked. A date of completion and IOTN score at the completion of treatment must be present. Orthodontic Treatment Completions With Extractions (Orthodontic): This is a count of the number of orthodontic treatment completions submitted where the extractions box has been ticked on a FP17O. This is based on the orthodontic clinical data set as recorded in part 4 of the FP17O. % Orthodontic Treatment Completions With Extractions (Orthodontic): This is the number of orthodontic treatment completions submitted where the extractions box has been ticked on a FP17O / Orthodontic Treatment Completions expressed as percentage. Adult/Child Description: Adult/Child Patients are defined based on the patients’ age at the date of acceptance. An adult is defined as a patient aged 18 or over at the date of acceptance, a child is defined as a patient ages aged under 18 at the date of acceptance. Ad-hoc Official Statistics

Dataset Description

The dataset provides a monthly breakdown from July 2023 to October 2025 of dental activity carried out by dentists on behalf of the NHS in England. The dataset provides monthly breakdowns of dental courses of treatment by:

  • adults/children
  • treatment band
  • national, NHS region, and Integrated Care Board (ICB) geographies

Data is provided by ‘Treatment Month’ – the month a course of treatment is assigned to based on the date of completion or date of last visit (the date of last visit may be the treatment acceptance date).

As FP17s can be submitted or amended for treatment months after they have originally been reported, data provided for April 2025 to October 2025 should be treated as provisional. Data provided for July 2023 to March 2025 is final.

This dataset allows comparisons of dental activity delivered to be made over time at different geographies.

The dataset can be used to:

  • assess delivery of courses of treatment across ICBs
  • provide evidence for policy makers, commissioners, and local healthcare teams to support decision making and evaluation
  • enable transparency in tracking delivery of dental activity allowing for public accountability

The annual Dental Statistics England Official Statistics publication provides in-depth data and information relating to the delivery of dental services and should be used to understand the broader landscape of general dentistry in England. This data set is produced using the same methodologies and criteria as the official statistics, however there are small differences due to the way that some contracts are mapped to commissioning organisations over time.

Dental contract level information is also published monthly on the NHSBSA Open Data Portal and should be used if you require more granular information. However, the English Contractor Monthly General Dental Activity excludes activity relating to foundation dentists and contracts not paid by the NHSBSA.

The NHSBSA is not responsible for access to NHS dental treatment.

Overview of Service

Information about our NHSBSA Dental Data service can be found here on the NHSBSA Dental Data webpage: About - Dental Data - Themes - Open Data Portal BETA (nhsbsa.net)

Caveats

Information:

Treatment Month Definition

Data is provided by ‘Treatment Month’ – the month a course of treatment is assigned to based on the date of completion or date of last visit (the date of last visit may be the treatment acceptance date).

Information:

Provisional and Final Data Status

As FP17s can be submitted or amended for treatment months after they have originally been reported, data provided for April 2025 to October 2025 should be treated as provisional. Data provided for July 2023 to March 2025 is final.

Information:

Data Extraction Date

This data was extracted on 2026-02-17. Due to the use of 'Treatment Month' any data reproduced for this time-period after this date may not match the data provided.

Information:

Health and Justice Contract Coverage

Data for Health and Justice (prison) contracts is included in national and regional totals, as these contracts are commissioned by regional teams, not ICBs. Health and Justice data has been excluded from the ICB breakdowns, therefore ICB data will not reconcile to the regional or national data.

Information:

Provider Coverage

Data for foundation dentists and dental care practitioners is included within this data set.

Information:

Patient Age Determination

A patient's age is determined at the date of acceptance of an FP17.

Information:

Age Group Classification

Data provides a breakdown by adult, children or both.

Children are patients that are aged 17 and under at the date of acceptance for a course of treatment.

Information:

‘Other’ Treatment Band Definition

The treatment band of ‘other’ includes courses of treatment with a band of:

  • free
  • regulation 11 replacement appliance
  • domiciliary visits
  • treatments with an unknown band

Dataset Description

This dataset comprises information on dentists in England who were on the performers list and delivered NHS care in the financial years 2016-17 to 2022-23. It outlines the number of performers who delivered within different ranges of 'Units of Dental Activity' (UDA)

To see the National overview of this data, go to the National performer by unit of dental activity (UDA) delivery for financial years 2016-17 to 2022-23 dataset.

On 7 February 2024, the government and NHS England published the paper: 'Faster, Simpler and Fairer: Our Plan to Recover and Reform NHS Dentistry' (dental recovery plan), in which a commitment was made to consult on the proposal for a ‘tie-in’ to NHS dentistry for newly qualified dentists. The purpose of this dataset release is to better inform the public on the amount of NHS dentistry being delivered through UDAs by dentists, to support informed responses to this consultation: Proposal for a ‘tie-in’ to NHS dentistry for graduate dentists - GOV.UK.

Overview of Service

A UDA is in essence a unit of activity, and is used within NHS contracts to describe the value of a dental course of treatment. For example, a dentist performing an examination would claim one UDA, while a dentist performing a course of treatment to create a crown for a patient would claim 12 UDAs. ‘UDA’ has a consistent definition across all NHS dentistry contracts, and can therefore be used to assess activity delivered by different performers.

Dentists’ income from NHS care is funded by contracts negotiated with the NHS, structured around UDAs as a measurement of their activity, and the amount of care delivered. Whilst there is an agreed number of UDAs for a provider to deliver in their contract, not all providers deliver their full contracted activity.

For further information on UDAs and NHS dentistry: NHS Dental Statistics: Supporting information and publication guidance - NHS England Digital

Dataset Details

Data Source

NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) Data Warehouse.

Data Collection

The dataset is derived from FP17 forms which are submitted by dentists via the Compass system.

Time Periods

The data covers financial years 2016-17 to 2019-20 and 2021-22 to 2022-23.

Due to COVID-19, information on dental activity for 2020-21 is unavailable.
Dental practices closed in March 2020, offering only remote urgent care. This significantly reduced activity, patient numbers, finances, and treatments (FP17/FP17W claims). Reopening began June 8th, 2020 with safety measures. See here for further details.

Geography

This data is for England only.

Statistical Classification

Management Information – This is not an official statistic.

Caveats

Dentists Working Across Multiple Regions

Please note that if a dentist delivers UDAs in more than one region in England, they will be counted separately in each region that they performed in. This means that some dentists will appear twice in the regional data.

Regional and National Dataset Totals May Differ

Because some dentists are counted twice in the regional dataset, it is likely that the total number of dentists included in the national dataset will not equal the sum of those included in the regional dataset.

Inclusion of Overseas-Trained Dentists

Please note, that whilst the consultation on the proposal for a ‘tie-in’ to NHS dentistry is seeking views on a policy that would only apply to domestically trained dentists, this dataset also includes dentists who have qualified overseas.

Exclusion of Dentists Providing Only UOAs

Dentists that exclusively deliver units of orthodontic activity (UOAs) are not included in this data. It may be that some of the dentists included in the data may also deliver UOAs alongside the UDAs represented in this data.

[1] "2026-04-21T15:48:05.553480" #> #> $results[[5]]$name #> [1] "national-uda-by-performer-for-financial-years-2016-2024" #> #> $results[[5]]$notes #> [1] "## Dataset Description This dataset comprises information on dentists in England who were on the performers list and delivered NHS care in the financial years 2016-17 to 2022-23. It outlines the number of performers who delivered within different ranges of 'Units of Dental Activity' (UDA) To see this data broken down by region, please go to the [Regional performer by unit of dental activity (UDA) delivery for financial years 2016-17 to 2022-23](https://opendata.nhsbsa.net/dataset/regional-uda-by-performer) dataset. On 7 February 2024, the government and NHS England published the paper: ['Faster, Simpler and Fairer: Our Plan to Recover and Reform NHS Dentistry'](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/our-plan-to-recover-and-reform-nhs-dentistry) (dental recovery plan), in which a commitment was made to consult on the proposal for a ‘tie-in’ to NHS dentistry for newly qualified dentists. The purpose of this dataset release is to better inform the public on the amount of NHS dentistry being delivered through UDAs by dentists, to support informed responses to this consultation: [Proposal for a ‘tie-in’ to NHS dentistry for graduate dentists - GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/proposal-for-a-tie-in-to-nhs-dentistry-for-graduate-dentists).

Overview of Service

A UDA is in essence a unit of activity, and is used within NHS contracts to describe the value of a dental course of treatment. For example, a dentist performing an examination would claim one UDA, while a dentist performing a course of treatment to create a crown for a patient would claim 12 UDAs. ‘UDA’ has a consistent definition across all NHS dentistry contracts, and can therefore be used to assess activity delivered by different performers.

Dentists’ income from NHS care is funded by contracts negotiated with the NHS, structured around UDAs as a measurement of their activity, and the amount of care delivered. Whilst there is an agreed number of UDAs for a provider to deliver in their contract, not all providers deliver their full contracted activity.

For further information on UDAs and NHS dentistry: NHS Dental Statistics: Supporting information and publication guidance - NHS England Digital

Dataset Details

Data Source

NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) Data Warehouse

Data Collection

The dataset is derived from FP17 forms which are submitted by dentists via the Compass system.

Time Periods

The data covers financial years 2016-17 to 2019-20 and 2021-22 to 2022-23.

Due to COVID-19, information on dental activity for 2020-21 is unavailable.
Dental practices closed in March 2020, offering only remote urgent care. This significantly reduced activity, patient numbers, finances, and treatments (FP17/FP17W claims). Reopening began June 8th, 2020 with safety measures. See here for further details

Geography

This data is for England only.

Statistical Classification

Management Information – This is not an official statistic.

Caveats

Dentists Working Across Multiple Regions

Please note that if a dentist delivers UDAs in more than one region in England, they will be counted separately in each region that they performed in. This means that some dentists will appear twice in the regional data.

Regional and National Dataset Totals May Differ

Because some dentists are counted twice in the regional dataset, it is likely that the total number of dentists included in the national dataset will not equal the sum of those included in the regional dataset.

Inclusion of Overseas-Trained Dentists

Please note, that whilst the consultation on the proposal for a ‘tie-in’ to NHS dentistry is seeking views on a policy that would only apply to domestically trained dentists, this dataset also includes dentists who have qualified overseas.

Exclusion of Dentists Providing Only UOAs

Dentists that exclusively deliver units of orthodontic activity (UOAs) are not included in this data. It may be that some of the dentists included in the data may also deliver UOAs alongside the UDAs represented in this data.

title: Show a dataset's metadata — nhsbsa_package_show
text: Wraps CKAN package_show action return full metadata single dataset, including list resources (downloadable files datastore tables).

title: Show a dataset's metadata — nhsbsa_package_show
code: nhsbsa_package_show(id, .return_raw = FALSE)

title: Show a dataset's metadata — nhsbsa_package_show
text: id Character scalar. dataset identifier name, returned nhsbsa_package_list(). .return_raw Logical. TRUE, return full parsed CKAN response envelope instead processed result. Defaults FALSE.

title: Show a dataset's metadata — nhsbsa_package_show
text: list dataset metadata. .return_raw = TRUE, parsed response envelope list.

title: Show a dataset's metadata — nhsbsa_package_show
code: metadata <- nhsbsa_package_show("english-prescribing-data-epd") metadata$title #> [1] "RETIRED - English Prescribing Dataset (EPD)"  # The dataset's resources (files / datastore tables) length(metadata$resources) #> [1] 138 metadata$resources[[1]]$name #> [1] "EPD_201401"

what: Perform a request against a CKAN action endpoint (internal) — nhsbsa_query
title: Perform a request against a CKAN action endpoint (internal) — nhsbsa_query
text: Builds request action, collecting query parameters calling endpoint function's arguments, performs retry/backoff returns parsed result element CKAN response envelope.

title: Perform a request against a CKAN action endpoint (internal) — nhsbsa_query
code: nhsbsa_query(action, call = rlang::caller_env())

title: Perform a request against a CKAN action endpoint (internal) — nhsbsa_query
text: action Character scalar. CKAN action call (e.g. "package_show"), appended base API path. call Environment report error messages.

title: Perform a request against a CKAN action endpoint (internal) — nhsbsa_query
text: result element CKAN response, — calling function invoked .return_raw = TRUE — full parsed response envelope.

title: Show a resource's metadata — nhsbsa_resource_show
text: Wraps CKAN resource_show action return metadata single resource (file datastore table).

title: Show a resource's metadata — nhsbsa_resource_show
code: nhsbsa_resource_show(id, .return_raw = FALSE)

title: Show a resource's metadata — nhsbsa_resource_show
text: id Character scalar. resource identifier. .return_raw Logical. TRUE, return full parsed CKAN response envelope instead processed result. Defaults FALSE.

title: Show a resource's metadata — nhsbsa_resource_show
text: list resource metadata. .return_raw = TRUE, parsed response envelope list.

title: Show a resource's metadata — nhsbsa_resource_show
code: resources <- nhsbsa_list_resources("english-prescribing-data-epd") meta <- nhsbsa_resource_show(resources$id[[1]]) meta$name #> [1] "EPD_201401" meta$datastore_active #> [1] FALSE

title: List tags — nhsbsa_tag_list
text: Wraps CKAN tag_list action list tags applied datasets. tags shown portal website; can filter datasets tag nhsbsa_package_search() (see vignette("nhsbsa")).

title: List tags — nhsbsa_tag_list
code: nhsbsa_tag_list(query = NULL, vocabulary_id = NULL, .return_raw = FALSE)

title: List tags — nhsbsa_tag_list
text: query Character scalar. Restrict results tags containing string. vocabulary_id Character scalar. Restrict results tags particular CKAN tag vocabulary. .return_raw Logical. TRUE, return full parsed CKAN response envelope instead processed result. Defaults FALSE.

title: List tags — nhsbsa_tag_list
text: character vector tags. .return_raw = TRUE, parsed response envelope list.

title: List tags — nhsbsa_tag_list
code: # All tags tags <- nhsbsa_tag_list() length(tags) #> [1] 1046  # Only tags containing a given string nhsbsa_tag_list(query = "prescribing") #>  [1] "English Prescribing Data"   "Prescribing"                #>  [3] "Hypnotic Prescribing Data"  "prescribing data"           #>  [5] "Prison Prescribing"         "prescribing"                #>  [7] "Prescribing data"           "secondary care prescribing" #>  [9] "Hospital Prescribing"       "Dental prescribing"         #> [11] "Prescribing Data"

title: nhsbsa 0.1.0
text: Initial release: low-level client NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) Open Data Portal, CKAN data catalogue. Dataset endpoints: nhsbsa_package_list(), nhsbsa_package_show() nhsbsa_package_search(). Resource endpoints file download: nhsbsa_resource_show(), nhsbsa_list_resources() nhsbsa_download_resource(). Datastore row queries: nhsbsa_datastore_search() nhsbsa_datastore_search_sql(). Catalogue listings: nhsbsa_organization_list(), nhsbsa_group_list() nhsbsa_tag_list().
